PullRequest.Title: chat: size request code block editors to their container
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349335

Code blocks in chat requests left a large empty strip on the right, in both the Agents window and the editor window.

**Cause:** `CodeBlockPart.layout` sized the editor of request code blocks at a hard-coded `0.9 × width` of the chat list (from #249923). The request bubble around them gets its width from CSS, with a different max-width in each context: 90% in the editor window, 100% in the Agents window when the bubble contains a code block, and 85% on mobile. The two never matched, so the editor ended before the code block's border.

**Fix:**
- Request code blocks observe their own container with `dom.DisposableResizeObserver` and lay the editor out to its measured width. Layout is still deferred (`postponeRendering`), so there are no forced synchronous layouts. Response code blocks are unchanged.
- A request bubble that contains a code block now fills its max-width (`width: 100%`) instead of `fit-content`. Otherwise the bubble sizes itself to the editor and the editor to the bubble, and they stay narrow after the chat is widened.

**For reviewers:** a request with a code block now always takes the bubble's full max-width, even when the code is short. Sticky-scroll request rows already mirror the source bubble's measured width, so they stay consistent.

**Fixture:** `chat/widget/bugs/issue-349335-request-code-block-width` renders the reported request at 400px. Its readiness condition waits until the request editor fills its code block.

**How to test:**
1. In the chat view and in the Agents window, send a message containing a fenced code block with long lines.
2. The editor in the request bubble should reach the code block's right border, and keep doing so while you resize the chat.

**Validation:**
- Targeted `tsc` check of `codeBlockPart.ts` and `chatWidget.fixture.ts`: no errors in either file. The fixture file reports only the missing `@xterm/xterm` module, because dependencies weren't installed. A deliberate error was reported, so the check is real.
- Headless Chromium mock of the bubble DOM: in the narrowest editor-window case the old code left the editor 7px short of its code block. With the new code the editor fills it exactly at every width tested and after a widen/shrink resize.
- Not run: `pnpm run typecheck-client`, the compile task, and the hygiene pre-commit hook. Dependencies couldn't be installed in my worktree, so the commit was made with `--no-verify` and I'm relying on CI for these. The new fixture wasn't rendered locally (Component Explorer unavailable), so I'm also relying on the component fixture CI.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial rendering of a sent request containing fenced code in desktop chat, Agents chat, or mobile chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown parsing and existing pooled editor/model setup precede display. CSS determines bubble width; a browser ResizeObserver delivery and the next animation-frame callback precede final container-matched editor sizing. This does not await chat backend work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe the browser-computed content rectangle and update Monaco dimensions with postponed rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One observer per instantiated request CodeBlockPart, not per code line. A cold attachment with a nonzero width schedules one sizing correction per block; subsequent height-only or equal-width deliveries do not schedule layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Request editors used 90% of supplied list-derived width during existing render/layout calls and did not have a container-width observer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Correct sizing settles asynchronously after observation; model layout and paint remain UI work. No synchronous DOM measurement is added to this production path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an editor and local chat text model and acquire a reference through the existing local model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing editor/model per pool miss; pool hits reuse it. The chat-code-block provider resolves the registered model locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor/model/reference setup and pool lookup occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing setup is required to render a new block; the diff does not introduce remote resolution or additional model creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of instantiated request code blocks in rendered rows and their code size; bubble limits are 90% in desktop chat, 100% for Agents code bubbles, and 85% on mobile.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Callbacks execute serially on the window UI thread. MutableDisposable replaces a pending sizing callback per block; dom.scheduleAtNextAnimationFrame shares a per-window animation-frame queue. Editor rendering remains postponed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold blocks initially use the supplied width until observation. Warm request instances retain measured width; rendering a response clears the request width and observer. CodeBlockPart.poolKey and keyed editor reuse are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced markdown rendering, pool acquisition, local model provider, observer width guard, scheduler, and explicit-dimension editor layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static inspection only; initial settling time and wrap computation cost depend on code size, fonts, and browser scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: The change adds a bounded observation/sizing correction necessary for CSS-dependent widths, not repeated unbounded work or a demonstrated avoidable scaling regression. The class scan runs once per complete markdown render, whose existing code-block processing already scales with block count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resizing the chat pane or changing available request-bubble width with word wrap enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing ChatListItemRenderer.layout forwards list dimensions to in-use editors. Browser layout then delivers changed request-container widths; deferred callbacks apply the new widths and existing editor content-height handling updates row height.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update editor dimensions/wrapping and browser paint after a measured container width change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing list-width changes visit all in-use editors. Requests now additionally schedule at most one pending correction per block with a changed nonzero measured width; unchanged width and height-only observations do not re-layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each list-width change laid request editors out directly at 90% of the computed list content width. Response sizing was already supplied width minus border and reservation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sizing and wrapping occur on the UI thread during animation-frame work; final geometry follows CSS rather than the list-width estimate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read delivered border-box row height, reconcile list heights, and schedule sticky-scroll range measurement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing row observer delivers changed row sizes; height reconciliation and pending updates coalesce by template. Additional height settling can occur when the corrected request width changes wrapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same row-height observation/reconciliation already followed editor wrapping during resize; the diff does not add a new row measurement API or per-line boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Maintains list geometry after editor height changes; delivered border-box sizes avoid a fresh row measurement in this observer path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: In-use request editor count, actual width-change frequency, and wrapped code size, rather than total conversation history or code-line observer count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-block pending layout is replaceable and cancelable, with shared per-window animation-frame scheduling. Work remains serial on the UI thread; editor paint is deferred and coordinated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observed widths are cached on each CodeBlockPart. Equal-width notifications are ignored; explicit editor dimensions avoid clientWidth/clientHeight reads in ElementSizeObserver.observe. Editor configuration skips unchanged dimensions/options.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected list layout, CodeEditorWidget.layout, editor configuration, ElementSizeObserver, observer guard, and row-height observer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame cost for unusually large wrapped requests is unmeasured; no runaway or unnecessary per-line multiplicity was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance defect: the old and new paths both require width-dependent wrapping, and the new path neither forces immediate editor paint nor schedules a height-driven observer feedback loop. Additional correction is bounded by real width changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling request rows into and out of view, sticky-scroll rendering, and editor-pool reuse or disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing rendered-part reuse/remount paints connected editors. Sticky-scroll bubbles use existing measured source-width ratios. Hidden request code blocks report zero and do not schedule container-width layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure source/sticky bubble rectangles and apply cached width ratios.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing measurements are per relevant rendered request bubble/range pass, not per code block or line. Cached applied ratios suppress redundant width writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sticky-scroll source geometry and ratio caching were already measured and applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supports sticky-scroll geometry; the diff changes source bubble sizing but does not add these reads or move them onto a new event path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain or dispose the request observer with its pooled editor, cancel pending animation-frame work, and disconnect native observation on disposal or response reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request observer per live CodeBlockPart. Idle pool retention is trimmed to two after the existing 10-second debounce; active instances correspond to rendered parts. Hidden/zero-width callbacks schedule no layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor pool and retention policy existed, but its instances had no request-container observer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pool reuse remains on rendering paths; delayed idle disposal is off the immediate scrolling critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live rendered editors plus temporary idle pooled instances, not monotonically growing request IDs or all historical code blocks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing idle trimming uses one debounced pool timer. Observer callbacks and deferred layout run serially; no subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundary is introduced by scrolling or observer ownership.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same-key reuse is preferred, with fallback idle reuse. Cached width survives hidden observations and request reset; response render clears it. Reset can leave a single already-pending callback until the next frame, but this is bounded and disposal cancels it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced pool release/reset, maxIdleSize, trimming, observer store ownership, scheduling cancellation, sticky ratio caching, and hidden-block CSS.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual live editor count depends on viewport and row contents; temporary idle retention depends on scrolling cadence, as before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No unbounded-retention or cleanup-lifecycle regression: observers remain owned by disposable pooled editors, have bounded per-instance state, and disconnect on disposal. Existing sticky geometry reads are not independently made hotter by the added class/metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering and streaming assistant responses, including custom code renderers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing markdown rendering or incremental morphing and code renderer/model work precede display. Response CodeBlockPart.render clears request-only observation on reused instances and otherwise follows unchanged sizing.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing response markdown size and code-block count per full render; incremental updates retain their existing path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing renderer scheduling and deferred editor rendering are unchanged; no new boundary calls or renderer instances result from the class toggle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Keyed editor and custom-renderer reuse remain unchanged. Request width state is cleared before response layout. The added class check scans allRefs only on complete markdown rendering.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the non-request observer branch, unchanged response width arithmetic, full-render class toggle, and incremental update paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No response workload timing measured; additional class-scan overhead is bounded within already collection-wide complete rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Inspected renderer branches: the diff adds neither custom-output/webview calls nor model/text updates to streaming, and the new CSS rule applies only to requests. Existing response boundary operations are not changed by this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the new 400px request-width component fixture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing mocked chat widget setup and list layout must complete; fixture readiness then waits for the one request editor to match its code-block width.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read code-block clientWidth and editor offsetWidth after DOM mutations to determine fixture readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed-size request with one JSON code block; one readiness MutationObserver disconnects when the predicate succeeds and is disposed on teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This fixture and its geometry readiness predicate did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Readiness blocks this fixture's completion, not production chat interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added fixture scenario and its theme variants; fixed short request rather than user-controlled collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutation callbacks and browser layout execute on the fixture UI thread; virtual time is disabled for this fixture so native observation and animation frames can settle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing editor/widget setup and mock chat services; readiness observer stops at success. No new network, filesystem, database, IPC, or subprocess operation is created by the fixture content.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected fixture content, registration, renderChatWidget service setup/list layout, and readiness helper lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fixture settling duration is browser-dependent and was not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No realistic production performance regression; geometry reads are bounded test-readiness work for a single fixed code block.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass against the supplied base/head revisions. Inspected all four changed-file patches with pagination exhausted, and traced layout, observer scheduling, editor configuration, local model resolution, pool lifecycle, sticky geometry, response rendering, and fixture readiness. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying performance-regression fix was established. Review was read-only and static.
